newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close softer, eye on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close softer, eye on U.S. data.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended weaker in an early close on Monday, with a flatter bond yield curve as investors eyed a slew of coming U.S data, analysts said.

"The curve is flattening because people think the Bank (of Canada) is near the end of its rate cuts," said MMS International analyst Rob Palombi. Canada's central bank dropped its key bank rate for the 11th time this year on Friday, cutting by 25 basis points to 3.25 percent.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.03 to C$115.43 to yield 6.743 percent. U.S. Treasury markets were closed for the Veterans Day holiday.
Canada's bond market closed early at 1400 EST/1900 GMT after a quiet day due to the Remembrance Day bank and government holiday.
Palombi added that investors were selling their short-term treasuries to buy long bonds, which provide higher yields. "The general trend is for the long end to outperform the short," he said.

North American markets will be busy this week with U.S. economic data and a U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Wednesday. Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen will present his semi-annual monetary policy report on Thursday.
"I think we'll get plenty of chances for volatility," one trader said.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent of 2006 dipped C$0.15 to C$106.17 to yield 6.166 percent. Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.88 percent.
